angle: Low-risk launch and prologue cuts for Engine A v6 at T=1 (decode 1). Five items in scope: K1's x staging against build_map, the record split's 64-bit divisions, build_map and its __syncthreads, where griddepcontrol launch_dependents and wait sit across K1 -> K2 -> combine, and the prologue's instruction-fetch footprint. Each is sized three ways: against P3c's per-PC data (ncu, standalone, H100), against M09 (production, a = 12.5 us + 10.2 us per local expert), and against the judge's own v6 anatomy and race lines (fd0e9271, be4440e2). I reread the P3c per-PC source CSV (runs/20261027-232407-gpunode06/.../ncu.source.csv) for this design. That reread changes two of P3c's lever sizes and adds one lever.
summary:
1) The x / h staging is a waterfall, not a latency. In the P3c SASS, b_copy is 8 serialized ELECT / R2UR / UBLKCP iterations plus a runtime k/T division (K1 +0x06010-0x064b0). It costs 1,019 cycles in K1 and 922 in K2, mostly 'wait' stalls (no_inst only 6 of 45 samples). In K1 it runs before issue(0), so record 0's copies start about 1,000 cycles late. The bfull wait itself (2,201 cycles) is never exposed, because record 0 lands 2,530 cycles after x does. So P3c's lever 3 is worth about 0.57 us, not 1.2. The fix is to take x off the producer's path.

2) K2 has the same waterfall right after griddepcontrol.wait. The judge's anatomy shows K2 'wait' +0.77 -> 'first' +1.79 us at n2 and +0.51 -> +1.54 at n3. That is about 1.0 us (4 ticks of 0.256 us) from the release to the consumers holding h.

3) New from the combine's SASS. ea_combine_kernel already hoists its 8 ids loads above griddepcontrol.wait (LDG.E.CONSTANT at +0x090, ACQBULK at +0x180; NVVM moves the __restrict__ const loads). But it sinks the norm-weight loads below the wait (+0x1f0 / +0x220) and issues the tw loads in the middle of the reduction (+0x1740). Both are cold in DRAM after the judge's L2 flush, so two DRAM trips run serially after the wait: about 0.9 us of the 2.5-3.8 us that M09 puts on the critical path.

4) Sized and not built:
   - 32-bit split: kept inside v6f, 416 -> about 120 cycles = -0.16 us in K1. K2's split runs under K1 in production, so it saves 0 there.
   - build_map + __syncthreads (1,421 cycles): this is warp 0's topk_ids DRAM latency (579 of 673 samples are barrier stalls). Only about 0.05 us can be cut.
   - Trigger placement is already right. An earlier K1 trigger would put K2's 9.7-MB prefetch against K1's 4.87-MB record-0 fill.
   - Entry cost (1,359 cycles: imc 318 + no_inst 272 of 742 samples) is cold fetch at launch. K2's and the combine's entries are hidden by PDL.

5) Build three raced arms, all bitwise identical to v6 by construction:
   - v6f: consumers stage x / h with __ldcg, the producer has no B waterfall, 32-bit K1 split. -1.4 us [0.85, 1.55].
   - v6c: the combine's w / tw / ids loads are pinned above the wait by empty asm volatile. -0.9 us [0.5, 1.1].
   - v6fc: both. -2.3 us [1.35, 2.65].
   The cuts are fixed-cost, so they apply at every k. M09's a goes 12.5 -> 11.1 / 11.6 / 10.2 us. On the judge, weighted with EA6_W1 against v6: x1.047 / x1.030 / x1.080. The decode-1 row drops 1.4 / 0.9 / 2.3 us, so the moe headline gains about +0.7 / +0.5 / +1.2% (geomean over 6 loads).
   The change uses no new PTX text. The only new device constructs are __ldcg on uint4 / int / float (already run on the judge in eb_kernels) and empty asm volatile. Size is about +10.5 KB (-> about 973 KB). Prepare grows 5-10 s. The v6 module adds 2 instances (+15-20 s in its background thread).
   If time is short, build v6c first: it is the smallest change and the largest single lever. Then v6f, then v6fc.

variants.name: v6f (FAST kernels: consumer-staged B, 32-bit K1 split)
variants.change:
rewrite/lib/cuda/ea6_kernels.cuh (namespace eak6), all new code under if constexpr so the four v6 instances compile as today.
(1) L33: template <bool W13, int D, int MINB, bool FAST = false>. Note in the L29-32 flags comment: 8 = FAST (T = 1 and MINB 2, checked on the host).
(2) After L53 (if (W13 && (flags & 4)) griddep_wait();) insert:
uint4 xb0 = make_uint4(0u, 0u, 0u, 0u), xb1 = xb0;
if constexpr (FAST && W13) { if (warp < 8) { uintptr_t pa = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(reinterpret_cast<const uint4*>(bsrc) + warp * 64); asm volatile("" : "+l"(pa)); xb0 = __ldcg(reinterpret_cast<const uint4*>(pa) + lane); xb1 = __ldcg(reinterpret_cast<const uint4*>(pa) + 32 + lane); } }
Each consumer warp loads its own 1 KB chunk of x (token 0, chunk = warp) at entry, while build_map's topk_ids load is in flight. The empty asm launders the pointer so no load of x can move above the optional decode griddep_wait.
(3) L73-76, K1 split: if constexpr (FAST) { const unsigned R = static_cast<unsigned>(NREC) * static_cast<unsigned>(n), Gu = static_cast<unsigned>(G); b = static_cast<int>(static_cast<unsigned>(c) * R / Gu); e = static_cast<int>(static_cast<unsigned>(c + 1) * R / Gu); } else { the 64-bit lines as they are }. The bound is (c+1)*512*n <= 1024*16384 = 2^24 (grid <= 1024 and count <= 32 are checked on the host), so the result is exact and identical. K2's split is unchanged.
(4) Producer: L124 b_copy(bsrc) -> if constexpr (!FAST) b_copy(bsrc); and L133 -> if constexpr (!FAST) b_copy(bsrc + static_cast<size_t>(a) * T * eak::KDIM). Record 0's issue now starts right after the split. K2's producer keeps griddep_wait(); dme[5]; griddep_launch(); in that order (this ordering is what v6c's safety argument needs).
(5) Consumers: replace L149 mbar_wait(bfull, 0u, err, dead) with:
if constexpr (FAST) { if (!W13) { uintptr_t pa = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(reinterpret_cast<const uint4*>(bsrc + static_cast<size_t>(a) * eak::KDIM) + warp * 64); asm volatile("" : "+l"(pa)); xb0 = __ldcg(reinterpret_cast<const uint4*>(pa) + lane); xb1 = __ldcg(reinterpret_cast<const uint4*>(pa) + 32 + lane); } uint4* d4 = reinterpret_cast<uint4*>(bsm + warp * eak::XROW); d4[lane] = xb0; d4[32 + lane] = xb1; __syncwarp(); } else { mbar_wait(bfull, 0u, err, dead); }
K2's consumers load h right after their own griddep_wait / griddep_launch; the laundered pointer keeps those loads below the wait. Both kernels write exactly the bytes b_copy wrote (row kc = warp, t = 0, at warp*1040, 1024 B). Each warp reads only its own rows, so __syncwarp is enough. bfull is still initialized but never armed or waited on.

variants.risk:
Low.
- Bitwise identical to v6 by construction: the same bytes reach smem, the CTAs get the same records, the fp32 order is the same.
- It removes one wait (bfull) and adds none. The protocol is v6's minus bfull, so there is no new deadlock path.
- Only judge-run forms: __ldcg(const uint4*) as in eb_kernels.cuh:662, uint4 smem stores, and an empty asm volatile.
- A compile error would take down the whole v6 module (T=1 -> v1 for that check). Mitigation: ea6_emul --src (g++ on the assembled module) and cuda_syntax. Both idioms parse under the stub; I checked that in this session.
- Registers: the 8 extra live registers sit only in prologue paths, not in the consume loop. The stage offers FAST only when rows 4 and 5 show 0 spill, occupancy >= 1, and the K1f + K2f pair still co-resides (10*alloc(r13f) + 10*alloc(r2f) <= 65,536).
- Mechanism: if record 0's DRAM fill or h's L2 latency weighs more than modeled, the gain shrinks toward 0.5-0.8 us. That is still above the 1.01 margin. The v6f anatomy line (K1 ramp, K2 first - wait) shows which half delivered.

rewrite/lib/cuda/ea_combine.cuh (main Engine A module).

Low-moderate.

- It touches the main Engine A module. A compile error there turns every Engine A path to master for that check, a bigger blast radius than v6f. Mitigation: keep <false> verbatim, g++-check _EA2_SRC, and text-check that the <false> path equals the board's kernel once the EARLY blocks are removed.

determinism_and_rules:
Determinism
- v6f, v6c and v6fc produce outputs bitwise identical to v6.
  - v6f moves the same bf16 bytes into the same smem B rows, using plain 16-B L2 loads and stores instead of TMA.
  - The 32-bit split gives identical record ranges: products are below 2^24, and the emulator asserts equality for G up to 1024 and n up to 32.
  - consume<2>, the epilogue and the fp32 order ((p0+p1)+...+p7, acc0+acc1) are untouched.
  - v6c loads the same ids, tw and w values earlier. Its arithmetic is token-for-token the <false> kernel's.
- So v6's guarantees carry over: bitwise repeats, the two-state copy check, rel-L2 against fp32. The canary prints a '=v6 bitwise k/n' count as a diagnostic, not as a gate.
- No buffers, counters, tickets or atomics are added. Nothing persists across calls.

Ordering and memory safety
- FAST K2's h loads follow the consumers' own griddepcontrol.wait. The pointer is laundered through an empty asm volatile that is ordered after the wait asm, and the loads are __ldcg (ld.global.cg, L2-coherent). Neither NVVM nor ptxas can hoist them above the wait.
- FAST K1's x loads use the same idiom, so they also stay below the optional decode griddep_wait.
- EARLY combine. Every v6 K2 thread calls launch_dependents only after its own griddepcontrol.wait, in all four paths. PDL counts a CTA's trigger at the first invocation, so the combine cannot start before K1 has completed. Then:
  - local_ids (written by K1's CTA 0) is final;
  - tw is a graph input in moe (the router's output in decode, finished before K1);
  - w is a prepare constant.
  The __ldcg loads read L2, so no stale L1 line is possible.
- Only v6c and v6fc pass pdl bit 2.
- Pre-existing, not introduced here: the board's combine already reads ids before the wait in every engine, via NVVM hoisting. For v1..v5 that is formally racy because their K2 triggers at entry. It has held in every canary and copy check, but the main thread should know.

Rules checklist (the attempt file's format)
- Graph-capturable. The same cudaLaunchKernelEx calls with a prepare-set flags bit. The fast bits are closure constants of each core. kernel_fn branches only on T and ea['on'][1]. No host syncs, no allocation from data, no control flow on input values. The two new TORCH_CHECKs test only T, minb and flags.
- Nothing derived from data is cached.
- Weights stay the existing lossless NVFP4 repack (w13r / w2r).
- fp32 accumulation and bf16 activations are unchanged, and outputs equal v6's, which are within the judge's tolerance.
- Copy checks are deterministic, with no fp32 atomics.
- All work is inside kernel_fn. The races, canary, anatomy and copy checks run in prepare only.
- Prepare stays under 300 s: the judge's 126 s plus 5-10 s.
- Size about 973 KB, under 990,000 B.
- Raced against v6 inside _ea6_stage. A loss, failure, deadline miss or copy-check miss leaves v6.
- PATH lines name the arm ('[engineA] PATH CHOSEN T=1 = ENGINE A v6fc').
- No timing patches, harness access, module edits, reference import, new processes beyond the existing load_inline builds, or network.
- First line kept; run under 15 min.
race_wiring:
All in rewrite/lib/ea6_core.py unless noted.

(1) Constants after EA6_FLOOR8:
- EA6F_ON = True.
- EA6F_MARGIN = 1.01: the EA6_W1-weighted v6/arm ratio must clear this in every round.
- EA6F_FLOOR = 0.99: every n = 1..5 must clear this in every round, because these arms are bitwise v6 and may not lose anywhere.
- EA6F_ARMS = {'v6f': 3, 'v6c': 4, 'v6fc': 7}. Bits: 1 = K1 FAST, 2 = K2 FAST, 4 = EARLY combine.

(2) _ea6_judge(per, specs, arms, margin=RT_MARGIN, tight=RT_MARGIN_TIGHT_IQR) with ok = floor_ok and (wr >= margin or (wr >= tight and iqr_ok)). Existing callers are unchanged.

(3) Admission in _ea6_stage, after MINB and cores:
- rows = [info[6*i:6*i+6] for i in range(len(info)//6)].
- fast = EA6F_ON and minb == 2 and cores and len(rows) >= 6 and all(rows[i][0] and rows[i][5] >= 1 and rows[i][2] == 0 for i in (4, 5)) and 10*alloc(rows[4][1]) + 10*alloc(rows[5][1]) <= 65536.
- farms = tuple(a for a, bits in EA6F_ARMS.items() if (fast or not bits & 3) and (ea.get('cmb_ok') or not bits & 4)), or () when EA6F_ON is off.
- ea['ea6_fast'] = fast.
- The build line appends '; FAST K1 r/l/o K2 r/l/o; fast arms ...' (stays within 199 chars).

(4) Canary: _ea6_canary(..., farms).
- At T=1, arms = ('v6', 'v6s') + farms, 2 reps each for the fast arms (bitwise repeat), core = _EA6_CORES[arm].
- bad, worst and first gain the fast keys.
- For each input, keep outs[0] of each good arm and count torch.equal against v6.
- One extra line: '[ea6] canary fast T=1: v6f clean (worst x, =v6 bitwise k/n); ...'.

node_ab_plan:
Setup
- Bytes: the new build (campaign/eb-fc).
- One cold, judge-shaped process per replicate on gpunode06, one pool GPU per replicate (R4), 2 replicates on distinct GPUs, at about 1830 MHz.

Arms (ea.on.1 overrides after prepare, same bytes)
- t1v6: the control, i.e. the board's T=1 path, untouched in this build.
- t1v6f, t1v6c, t1v6fc.
- 'same': the build's own routing; expected to pick v6fc.
- Optional attribution: cores with fast bits 1 / 2 (K1-only / K2-only), if exposed.
- Cross-bytes control: board 81c9802e with t1v6. It must match this build's t1v6 within the 0.45% MDE, which shows the v6 instances and the <false> combine are unchanged.

Shapes
- decode 1 (T=1) BY_K, forced k (distinct local experts) in {0, 1, 2, 3, 4}, 1400 reps, 28 profiled.
- An nsys E3 split per k: K1, K1->K2 gap, K2, K2->combine gap, combine; fidelity tolerance 3%.
- The natural decode-1 row with judge-like routings.

Metric
- Per (arm, k): the replay median, with a cold-L2 read flush and the empty-graph baseline subtracted.
- Paired ratios t1v6/arm per k (R3a at the 0.45% MDE).
- OLS a + b*k over k >= 1 per arm, with bootstrap CIs; the k=0 floor separately.

Pre-registered expectation
- delta a(v6f) = +1.4 [0.85, 1.55] us.
- delta a(v6c) = +0.9 [0.5, 1.1] us, plus a k=0 floor 0.4-0.7 us lower.
- delta a(v6fc) = +2.3 [1.35, 2.65] us.
- |delta b| <= 0.2 us per expert.
- Mechanism, from the node's [ea6] lines: the v6f anatomy's K1 ramp is >= 0.4 us below v6's, and its K2 (first - wait) is <= 0.45 us against v6's ~1.0. The fast race line shows Q for the routed arm.

Decision rule
- An arm stays in the judge build if, in both replicates, every k in 1..4 has t1v6/arm >= 0.995 (no loss beyond the MDE).
- An arm is removed from EA6F_ARMS if any k reads < 0.99 in both replicates.
- If delta a(v6f) < 0.3 us in both replicates, the waterfall model is wrong: read nsys and the anatomy before spending a judge check on v6f. v6c can still ship on its own.
- Void below 1800 MHz, or on any check failure, canary FAIL or copy-check FAIL.

Correctness on the same bytes
- fuzz-odd, fuzz-skew and the 32-shape held-out sweep, as for S3.
- Optional read-only check: cuobjdump -sass of the built ea6 and Engine A extensions. The EARLY w / ids / tw LDGs should sit above ACQBULK, the FAST K2 h LDGs below the consumers' ACQBULK, and the FAST instances should show 0 spill.

Cost and timing
- About 10-12 GPU-min for the A/B plus about 6 min for correctness, inside the 13:40Z window.
- The judge check need not wait for this run, since the stage races the arms on the judge itself. But a compile or canary problem would show here first.
risks:
1. Compile failure wastes the check. In the v6 module, T=1 falls back to v1 (the decode-1 row loses ~6%). In the main module, through v6c's template, every Engine A path goes to master. Mitigation:
   - no new PTX text;
   - judge-run __ldcg forms only, plus empty asm volatile;
   - <false> kept verbatim and text-diffed against the board;
   - g++ stub checks of _EA2_SRC and the assembled v6 module.
   Residual risk is about 1-2%. If time is short, build v6c alone first.
2. Ordering relies on the compiler honouring volatile asm order around griddepcontrol.wait.
   - Hoisting FAST K2's h loads above the wait would corrupt outputs. The canary, bitwise repeats and copy check would catch it.
   - Sinking v6c's loads below the wait only loses the gain.
   - The optional node SASS dump confirms both.
3. Mechanisms could prove smaller than modeled:
   - record 0's fill may dominate K1;
   - L2 same-line contention across the 66-132 SMs that read one h may put __ldcg's latency near TMA's;
   - w / tw may survive the flush.
   Then each arm gains 0.3-0.8 us. The 1.01 margin and 0.99 floors reject anything smaller, v6 stays, and one check is spent. The anatomy (K1 ramp, K2 first - wait) and v6fc vs v6f show which part delivered.
4. Registers: FAST adds live registers only in prologue paths, and admission requires 0 spill and kept K1+K2 co-residency. The EARLY combine keeps nw / g / loc live across the wait. Its peak (squares, 187) should hold, but ea_combine_info reports only <false>, so a spill would show only as a slow v6c.
5. Safety invariants that must not change later:
   - pdl bit 2 only after v6's K2;
   - FAST only at T=1 with MINB 2 (host TORCH_CHECK);
   - v6's K2 trigger strictly after its wait in every path.
   Comment these at the code sites.
6. Pre-existing finding, not introduced here: the board's combine reads ids before griddepcontrol.wait for every engine (NVVM hoist). That is formally racy for v1..v5 at T <= 32, whose K2 triggers at entry. Flag it to the main thread.
7. Shared files: ea_combine.cuh is in decode's build, so build.py --check reports decode out of date. Regenerate it; behaviour is unchanged because decode passes pdl 0 or 1. Decode's main module compiles one more instance (+1-2 s).
8. Prepare and build: +5-10 s on the main thread. The v6 module build grows by about 15-20 s in its thread under CPU contention with the main / es1a builds. Expected margins are wide: the judge stage ends near 120-125 s against limits of 170 / 200 / 215 s.
9. Racing 3 arms with 'best worst-round wr' can pick a noise-equal arm. That is harmless: all arms are bitwise v6 and none may lose more than 1% at any n.
10. The judge's %globaltimer ticks at about 0.256 us, so the anatomy resolves the K1 and K2 deltas (2-3 ticks each) but not the split (< 1 tick).
11. The node harness's name parsing (racelines.py) must accept v6f / v6c / v6fc, or node arms will mislabel.
decode_port_notes:
Shared code. ea6_kernels.cuh (FAST instances, flags bit 8) and ea_combine.cuh (EARLY, pdl bit 2) are shared sources. eb-s3d's decode build picks both up unchanged:
- decode's v6 module gains 2 instances, about +15-20 s in its thread. Check that the join still lands before EAD6_START_S 95.
- decode's main module gains one combine instance, about +1-2 s.
- ea6_info grows to 6 rows. eb-s3d's parser reads rows by index and still works.

Core. ea_decode.py _ead6_forward_core takes the same fast bits:
- K1 stays plain (EAD_PLAIN_K1, flags 0) and ORs in 8 for bit 1.
- K2 keeps 1 | (2 if cores) and ORs in 8 for bit 2.
- The combine gets pdl 3 for bit 4, only when decode's combine gate kept the CUDA combine for v6.
The EARLY safety argument holds unchanged: the chain is router -> K1 (plain) -> K2 (PDL, triggers after its wait) -> combine (PDL).

Expected effect. In decode, x and topk_ids are L2-hot router outputs, so K1's prologue is shorter. Removing b_copy (~0.55 us) is then a larger share of the K1 ramp, and K2's h path saves the same ~0.7 us. EARLY: w is a cold prepare constant, and tw, the router output, is likely evicted by the ~73 MB of weights streamed since. Expect -0.5 to -0.9 us. The d1 layer (~98 us) should drop by 1.35-2.65 us, x1.014-1.028 on the d1 rows.

Stage (_ead6_stage). After v6 passes its per-n block race:
- race the fast arms against v6 in a block race with the EA6F rule;
- apply the whole-layer guard (fast arm vs v6 >= EAD6_GUARD 0.995, every round, both natural inputs);
- run the layer check;
- run the copy check with fallback to v6.
That adds about 3-5 s against EAD6_COPY_S 112 (the stage ends around 117 s now). Re-budget EAD6_GATE_S / EAD6_COPY_S, or port only the arm the moe check routed (likely v6fc) to save time.

Size: 966,613 + ~2.6 KB (kernel) + ~1.9 KB (combine) + ~3.5 KB (stage) ≈ 974.6 KB, under 990,000.
